**Finding submitted: deviation (EXCLUSIVITY), fallback target.**

**What we found**
- **Section 6.1 (p0037)** is the operative exclusivity clause and it binds *us*: for the term we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or substantially similar products, and HDI holds the exclusive right to use the "Deerskin" brand for a direct-to-consumer site.
- **Section 4.1 (p0024)** auto-renews the term annually unless 90 days' notice is given, so the restriction can run indefinitely — well beyond the 12-month fallback cap.
- The only relief is the closeout carve-out in **6.2 (p0040–p0041)** and the Globix transition acknowledgement in **9(b) (p0058)**; **1.6 (p0011)** gives only a right to terminate the whole Agreement if the Site is not live in 70 days. There is **no performance-based exit from the exclusivity itself** — walk-away territory.
- **Section 6.3 (p0042)** is HDI's reciprocal restriction, which benefits us; left untouched, and used only as the anchor for the new clause.

**Redline (validated ok:true, minimality gate passed)**
1. p0037: "during the term of this Agreement" → "for twelve (12) months from the Effective Date" (caps duration for both limbs of the sentence).
2. New 6.4 after p0042: "The exclusivity provided in Section 6.1 shall terminate automatically upon HDI's failure to meet any service level or delivery date required under this Agreement."

**Element coverage:** defined product category already met by the existing "Deerskin Products" scope; the 12-month cap and both automatic-exit triggers are carried by the two operations. We did not press the preferred position (outright deletion) given the cost-bearing bargain and HDI's own non-compete.
